Definition: from G1909 and G4936; to hasten together upon one place (or a particular occasion):--come running together.
BiblicalUsage: Episyntrecho means to run together, to hasten to one place — and when Jesus saw that the people came running together, He rebuked the foul spirit, saying, Thou dumb and deaf spirit, I charge thee, come out of him.
TheologicalSignificance: People hastening together, and Jesus acting before the crowd can settle: the running crowd is the scene of so many miracles.
RelatedEvents: The Healing of the Demon-Possessed Boy
